title: Zechariah Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 1.

questions.question: In which month and year did the word of the LORD come to Zechariah?
options: Eighth month, second year of Darius
Eleventh month, first year of Darius
Eighth month, first year of Cyrus
Tenth month, second year of Darius
questions.correctAnswer: Eighth month, second year of Darius
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:1 states the word of the LORD came in the eighth month, in the second year of Darius.

questions.question: Who is Zechariah's father according to Zechariah 1?
questions.correctAnswer: Berechiah
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:1 identifies Zechariah as the son of Berechiah.

questions.question: What has the LORD been with the fathers of the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Sore displeased
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:2 clearly says the LORD hath been sore displeased with your fathers.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do if the people turn to Him?
questions.correctAnswer: He will turn unto them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:3 says, 'Turn ye unto me... and I will turn unto you.'

questions.question: According to Zechariah 1, how did the fathers respond to the former prophets?
options: They did not hear nor hearken
questions.correctAnswer: They did not hear nor hearken
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:4 states that the fathers did not hear nor hearken unto the prophets.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets and the fathers live forever according to Zechariah 1.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:5 asks, 'Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, do they live forever?' implying they do not live forever.

questions.question: What did the fathers say about the dealings of the LORD towards them?
options: The LORD dealt with us according to our ways and doings
The LORD was unjust to us
The LORD saved us from all troubles
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD dealt with us according to our ways and doings
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:6 explains that the fathers said the LORD dealt with them according to their ways and doings.

questions.question: On what day and in which month did the LORD speak to Zechariah the second time in the second year of Darius?
options: Twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month
First day of the eighth month
Fifteenth day of the tenth month
Tenth day of the ninth month
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:7 states the word of the LORD came upon the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month.

questions.question: True or False: The man Zechariah saw by night was riding a white horse.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:8 says the man was riding a red horse, not white.

questions.question: What kind of trees were around the man riding the red horse?
questions.correctAnswer: Myrtle trees
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:8 mentions the man stood among the myrtle trees.

questions.question: What did the angel say these horses were sent to do?
options: Walk to and fro through the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Walk to and fro through the earth
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:10 says these horses were sent to walk to and fro through the earth.

questions.question: True or False: The earth was at rest when the horses walked to and fro according to Zechariah 1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:11 states that all the earth sitteth still and is at rest.

questions.question: How many years had the LORD had indignation against Jerusalem and the cities of Judah before the angel asked about mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy years
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:12 mentions the LORD had indignation these threescore and ten years, which is seventy years.

questions.question: Which comes first in Zechariah 1:3-4: the LORD commanding to turn unto Him or the LORD warning not to be like the fathers?
options: The LORD commanding to turn unto Him
The LORD warning not to be like the fathers
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD commanding to turn unto Him
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:3 commands to turn unto the LORD first, then Zechariah 1:4 warns not to be like the fathers.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah is called the son of Iddo in Zechariah 1.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah is the son of Berechiah, who is the son of Iddo, so Zechariah is not the son of Iddo directly (Zechariah 1:1).

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Zechariah see by night standing among the myrtle trees in the bottom?
options: A man riding upon a red horse
questions.correctAnswer: A man riding upon a red horse
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:8 states that he saw a man riding upon a red horse standing among the myrtle trees, indicating a vision of divine messengers.

questions.question: Who explained to Zechariah what the horses he saw represented?
options: The angel that talked with him
questions.correctAnswer: The angel that talked with him
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:9 records that the angel who talked with Zechariah said, 'I will shew thee what these be,' showing the angel’s role as interpreter.

questions.question: What are the horses that the LORD sent to walk to and fro through the earth?
options: They are heavenly messengers sent by the LORD
They are wild animals roaming the land
questions.correctAnswer: They are heavenly messengers sent by the LORD
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 1:10, the man among the myrtle trees states that the horses are those whom the LORD sent to walk through the earth, symbolizing divine agents.

questions.question: What did the horses report to the angel of the LORD about the condition of the earth?
options: All the earth sitteth still and is at rest
The earth is in turmoil and conflict
The earth is covered in darkness
The earth is flooded with water
questions.correctAnswer: All the earth sitteth still and is at rest
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:11 says the horses answered the angel that all the earth sits still and is at rest, indicating a period of quiet or peace.

questions.question: What question did the angel of the LORD ask concerning Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?
options: How long wilt thou not have mercy on them?
When will they be destroyed completely?
questions.correctAnswer: How long wilt thou not have mercy on them?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:12 records the angel asking the LORD how long He will withhold mercy on Jerusalem and Judah, showing concern for their restoration.

questions.question: How did the LORD respond to the angel's question about mercy on Jerusalem and Judah?
options: With good words and comfortable words
questions.correctAnswer: With good words and comfortable words
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:13 states the LORD answered the angel with comforting words, showing His intent to show mercy and restoration.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He is jealous for with a great jealousy?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem and Zion
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:14 reveals the LORD's great jealousy for Jerusalem and Zion, demonstrating His passionate care for His people and their city.

questions.question: What is the LORD's attitude toward the heathen that are at ease, according to the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Very sore displeased
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:15 states the LORD is very sore displeased with the heathen at ease, because their complacency helped forward affliction upon His people.

questions.question: Based on Zechariah 1:3 and 1:16, what is promised if the people turn unto the LORD?
options: The LORD will return to Jerusalem with mercies and rebuild His house
The LORD will punish them severely
The people will be scattered among nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will return to Jerusalem with mercies and rebuild His house
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:3 calls for turning unto the LORD, promising He will turn unto them, and 1:16 confirms the LORD’s return to Jerusalem with mercies to rebuild His house.

questions.question: How does this passage teach us about God’s faithfulness despite past disobedience?
options: God promises to restore Jerusalem and show mercy if His people repent
God ignores the prayers of His people
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to restore Jerusalem and show mercy if His people repent
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:3 urges the people to turn to God, and 1:16-17 shows God’s promise to return with mercies and comfort Zion, demonstrating His faithfulness.

questions.question: What do the four horns seen by Zechariah symbolize?
options: The powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem
The four corners of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:19 explains that the four horns represent those who scattered the people, symbolizing oppressive powers or nations.

questions.question: What is the role of the four carpenters seen by Zechariah in the vision?
options: To cast out the horns of the Gentiles who scattered Judah
To bring peace to the nations
To judge the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To cast out the horns of the Gentiles who scattered Judah
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:21 says the carpenters come to frighten and cast out the horns, meaning they act to remove the oppressing powers over Judah.

questions.question: True or False: The horses that the LORD sent were described as only red in color.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:8 describes red horses, but also mentions horses that were speckled and white, showing diversity in the vision.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's jealousy for Jerusalem and Zion shows His passionate care and desire for their welfare.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:14 declares the LORD’s great jealousy for Jerusalem and Zion, demonstrating His deep concern and protective love.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zechariah 1:12, the LORD had shown mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah continuously for seventy years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:12 indicates the LORD had shown indignation, not mercy, toward Jerusalem and Judah for seventy years, asking how long mercy would be withheld.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 1:15, why is the LORD very sore displeased with the heathen?
options: Because they were at ease and helped forward the affliction
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were at ease and helped forward the affliction
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:15 states the LORD was very sore displeased with the heathen because they were at ease and helped forward the affliction.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare He will do in Jerusalem according to Zechariah 1:16?
options: Return with mercies and have His house built
questions.correctAnswer: Return with mercies and have His house built
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:16 says the LORD will return to Jerusalem with mercies and His house shall be built there.

questions.question: What is promised about the cities of Judah in Zechariah 1:17?
options: They will be spread abroad through prosperity
They will be conquered by the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They will be spread abroad through prosperity
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:17 promises that the cities will be spread abroad through prosperity and the LORD will comfort Zion.

questions.question: In Zechariah 1:18, what vision does Zechariah see when he lifts up his eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: Four horns
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:18 records that Zechariah saw four horns when he lifted his eyes.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 1:19, what do the four horns represent?
options: The four corners of the earth
The horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:19 explains the four horns are those which scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the LORD show Zechariah in Zechariah 1:20 following the vision of the horns?
questions.correctAnswer: Four carpenters
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:20 states the LORD showed Zechariah four carpenters after the vision of the four horns.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the four carpenters as explained in Zechariah 1:21?
options: To fray and cast out the horns of the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: To fray and cast out the horns of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:21 explains the four carpenters come to frighten and cast out the horns of the Gentiles who scattered Judah.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book shares the theme of God's jealousy for Jerusalem and judgment on surrounding nations as seen in Zechariah 1:14-15?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 10:10 and 12:7 reflect God's jealousy for Zion and displeasure with nations at ease, paralleling Zechariah 1:14-15.

questions.question: The phrase 'my house shall be built' in Zechariah 1:16 foreshadows fulfillment in which New Testament event?
options: The establishment of the church as God's dwelling place
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of the church as God's dwelling place
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:16's promise of rebuilding God's house foreshadows the church as the spiritual temple in the New Testament (1 Corinthians 3:16).

questions.question: In Zechariah 1:15, the Hebrew word translated as 'displeased' is closely related to which of the following meanings?
questions.correctAnswer: Severe anger or wrath
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word used conveys strong displeasure or wrath, indicating God's intense anger with the heathen as in Zechariah 1:15.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Zechariah 1:18-21 to convey the message of judgment and restoration?
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolic vision
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:18-21 employs symbolic visions of horns and carpenters to represent nations and agents of judgment and restoration.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 1:16 indicates that the LORD will stretch a measuring line upon Jerusalem as a symbol of judgment only.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:16 indicates the LORD will stretch a line upon Jerusalem in the context of mercy and rebuilding, not judgment alone.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 1:17 assures that the LORD will comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem again.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:17 clearly states the LORD will comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem, affirming God's restoration plans.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Zechariah's theme of God’s jealousy and restoration of Jerusalem as seen in Zechariah 1:14 and 1:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 11:26-27
questions.explanation: Romans 11:26-27 reflects God's enduring covenant and mercy towards Israel, resonating with Zechariah 1:14 and 1:16’s themes of jealousy and restoration.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'four horns' and 'four carpenters' in the historical context of ancient Near Eastern symbolism as seen in Zechariah 1:18-21?
options: Horns symbolize power of nations; carpenters symbolize agents of divine judgment and restoration
Horns symbolize kings; carpenters symbolize builders of pagan temples
Horns represent animals; carpenters represent craftsmen only
Horns symbolize peace; carpenters symbolize war
questions.correctAnswer: Horns symbolize power of nations; carpenters symbolize agents of divine judgment and restoration
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern iconography, horns represent strength or powers (nations), and carpenters symbolize those who dismantle or rebuild, matching Zechariah 1:18-21.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Zechariah's command to "Turn ye unto me, and I will turn unto you"?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:3 shows God's willingness to restore relationship with His people if they repent, highlighting His mercy and readiness to forgive.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 1:5, what theological truth is taught about the prophets and the fathers?
options: The prophets and fathers live forever
The fathers and prophets do not live forever
The fathers are more important than the prophets
The prophets have ultimate authority over the fathers
questions.correctAnswer: The fathers and prophets do not live forever
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:5 teaches that both the fathers and the prophets are mortal, emphasizing human finitude and the continuing relevance of God's word rather than human authority.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is underscored by the phrase, "all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest," in Zechariah 1:11?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over the nations
questions.explanation: The quietness of the earth in Zechariah 1:11 reflects God's sovereign control over all nations, showing that worldly powers are under His dominion (cf. Psalm 22:28).

questions.question: How does Zechariah 1:14 reveal an attribute of God in His relationship to Jerusalem and Zion?
questions.correctAnswer: God's jealousy
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:14 explicitly states God is 'jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy,' highlighting His passionate commitment and protective love for His covenant people.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about divine judgment and mercy emerges from Zechariah 1:2-3 and Zechariah 1:15-16?
options: God's judgment is final and irreversible
God's judgment is coupled with the promise of restoration
God's mercy is limited to Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is coupled with the promise of restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 show God's displeasure and call to repentance, while verses 15-16 promise His return to Jerusalem with mercies, teaching that divine judgment invites repentance and leads to restoration.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the four horns and four carpenters in Zechariah 1:18-21?
options: The doctrine of divine judgment and deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment and deliverance
questions.explanation: The horns symbolize the powers that scattered Israel, while the carpenters represent God's agents to cast out those powers, illustrating God's sovereign judgment and deliverance (Zechariah 1:18-21).

questions.question: How does Zechariah 1:13-14 contribute to understanding God's communicative nature in prophecy?
options: God responds with harsh judgment only
God answers with comforting and clear words
questions.correctAnswer: God answers with comforting and clear words
questions.explanation: God's response in Zechariah 1:13 is described as 'good words and comfortable words,' showing that God communicates hope and reassurance through prophetic messages.

questions.question: What role does Zechariah 1:7 play in the narrative arc of the chapter concerning God's timing?
options: It announces the first word from God to Zechariah
It marks the divine word coming at a specific time during Darius' reign
It describes the end of prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the divine word coming at a specific time during Darius' reign
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:7 situates the prophetic vision within a historical timeframe, emphasizing God's sovereign timing in redemptive history.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's promises of restoration contradict His justice since He shows mercy to rebellious nations. What does Zechariah 1:15-17 actually teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God is unjust by showing mercy
God's mercy is a sign of weakness
God balances justice with mercy, acting against the complacent heathen but promising restoration to Jerusalem
God ignores justice in favor of mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God balances justice with mercy, acting against the complacent heathen but promising restoration to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:15-17 reveals God’s displeasure with the complacent heathen but also His merciful return to Jerusalem, demonstrating the harmony of divine justice and mercy (cf. Micah 7:18).

questions.question: What does Zechariah 1:8-10 reveal about God’s method of surveying and controlling the earth?
options: God is unaware of earthly affairs
God sends messengers who actively patrol and observe the earth
God leaves the earth to chance
God only intervenes through natural disasters
questions.correctAnswer: God sends messengers who actively patrol and observe the earth
questions.explanation: The red horses represent messengers sent by God to walk to and fro through the earth (Zechariah 1:8-10), illustrating God’s active governance of creation.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by Zechariah 1:6 about the response of the fathers to God's words and statutes through the prophets?
options: The fathers ignored God's words completely
The fathers repented and obeyed perfectly
The fathers acknowledged divine justice in their suffering
The fathers were justified by their works
questions.correctAnswer: The fathers acknowledged divine justice in their suffering
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:6 shows that the fathers accepted that God's judgments were deserved because of their ways, teaching the doctrine of divine justice and human accountability.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 1:16-17 connect to the broader redemptive story of Scripture concerning Jerusalem and Zion?
options: It foresees their restoration and God's ongoing covenant faithfulness
It denies God's interest in Zion
questions.correctAnswer: It foresees their restoration and God's ongoing covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: These verses promise mercies and comfort for Jerusalem and Zion, aligning with the biblical theme of God's covenantal restoration (cf. Isaiah 40:1-2).

questions.question: What biblical theological theme is highlighted by the question in Zechariah 1:19, "What be these?" regarding the four horns?
options: The theme of divine judgment against oppressors
The theme of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of divine judgment against oppressors
questions.explanation: The four horns are explained as the powers that scattered Judah and Israel, signifying God's judgment against oppressive nations (Zechariah 1:19).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth arises from Zechariah 1:4-6 and 1:12 regarding human response and God's patience?
options: God is impatient and punishes immediately
God's patience invites repentance but human stubbornness brings judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's patience invites repentance but human stubbornness brings judgment
questions.explanation: These verses show prophets calling to repentance which was ignored (1:4-6), and the angel asking how long God's mercy will delay due to persistent sin (1:12), teaching God's longsuffering and human responsibility.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 1:1 emphasize about the historical context of the prophetic word to Zechariah?
options: It was given during the exile in Babylon
It was given in the eighth month of Darius' second year, marking a post-exilic restoration period
It was delivered to King Darius himself
It was a generic prophecy with no historical markers
questions.correctAnswer: It was given in the eighth month of Darius' second year, marking a post-exilic restoration period
questions.explanation: Zechariah 1:1 situates the prophecy in a precise historical moment after the exile, pointing to the renewed hope for Judah's restoration under Persian rule.
